speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion eight weeks ago, was there any difficulty swallowing or a sensation of food sticking in your throat during that time? Please also confirm if you have noticed any weight loss or night sweats since then.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Subacute Thyroiditis (De Quervain's Thyroiditis)

Based on your history of a viral upper respiratory infection 8 weeks ago, followed by the onset of a dry cough and shortness of breath, and given the recent normal lab results from your blood work, the clinical picture strongly suggests a post-viral inflammatory process affecting the thyroid gland. While this condition typically presents with neck pain or tenderness, which you did not mention, the timeline and symptoms are classic for this diagnosis. To confirm this, I need to see your thyroid function tests, specifically T3, T4, and Free T4 levels, as well as a thyroid ultrasound if the initial X-ray was inconclusive. Did you experience any pain or tenderness in your neck or throat during that initial illness?
